reveWebLead.thirdPartyEvidence: @gasolinaradar/dgt-ev-collector 1.5.1 documents live-tested public-map behavior, embedded tariffs/status and the same normalized consumer output shape for public and external sources. Its public documentation also exposes a live side-by-side comparison command against the external API and states that connectorId/evseId are the reliable keys relating normalized prices and availability.
reveWebLead.grossNetNormalizationEvidence: Matched examples strongly indicate the public-map representation is consumer-facing VAT-inclusive/rounded while the external API retains net price components plus vat=21. Examples: 0.8265*1.21≈1.00, 4.956*1.21≈6.00 and 0.566*1.21≈0.68. This explains at least part of the apparent raw/naive semantic mismatches but is not yet proof for all 32 matches.
reveWebLead.parityInterpretation: Raw or path-sensitive semantic inequality is not evidence of price disagreement. A VAT-aware component comparator must pair component type, step size, restrictions and dates before deciding equivalence. Public availability also cannot be compared directly to the bulk external operational_status boolean without identifier/semantic mapping.
reveWebLead.nextSafeStep: Run a VAT-aware component comparator over the bounded connector-ID overlap and resolve EVSE availability against the appropriate external identifier/status representation. Do not run a national public sweep or promote this source yet.
